extracted.intended_audience: power sector stakeholders (utilities, generators), state agencies, regulated entities, and commenters on EPA rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and considerations EPA uses to identify the Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER) and assess feasible, cost-reasonable controls for fossil-fuel electric generating units (steam boilers and combustion turbines). Applies to evaluating technologies, timing, costs, and regulatory context for emission standards under CAA section 111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) feasibility and cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of CCS based on current state and cost of CCS technology for use with steam generating units and stationary combustion turbines; review reflected in BSER discussions and detailed in RIA and final TSDs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider existence of pilot projects, FEED studies, and techno-economic analyses (e.g., Linde/BASF 10 MW pilot; NETL base case comparisons) that indicate potential capital cost reductions relative to baseline cases. Assess whether projects are technically viable and cost-reasonable to deploy for the affected units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project development status and deployment timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether CCS or other control projects have completed FEED studies or are in advanced stages of development such that they can be built and commence operation within the relevant compliance timeframe (e.g., before January 1, 2032).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence of completed FEED studies, advanced development status, and construction timelines as evidence of deployability. Explicitly consider calendar deadlines for tax/credit eligibility and rule compliance windows when assessing feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated capture performance (capture rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance targets or demonstrated capture percentages for CCS projects (for example, NET Power designing to achieve greater than 97 percent CO2 capture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reported or designed CO2 capture rates from projects and pilots as indicators of technical effectiveness; factor capture design capacity requirements in incentive statutes when considering practical deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas co-firing capability and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitution of natural gas for some coal so the unit fires a combination of coal and natural gas ("natural gas co-firing"); modification typically involves new gas burners, boiler modifications, and possibly pipeline construction; costs have declined with narrowing coal/gas price differentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether existing boilers can be modified to co-fire at desired proportions, estimate capital costs (burner installation, pipeline), and consider recent reductions in expected costs. Use reported unit practices (e.g., number of units using gas) to infer technical feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational evidence of co-firing capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical operational data (hourly reported CO2 emission rates) indicating that units co-fire at specific rates (example: 29 units co-fired at or above 60 percent of capacity on an hourly basis from 2015–2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hourly emissions and fuel reporting to infer actual co-firing capability and required extent of burner/pipeline modifications. Operational data showing sustained high co-fire rates indicate technical capability at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient generation as BSER for combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly efficient generation (for simple cycle and combined cycle combustion turbines) is identified as BSER for certain new and reconstructed stationary combustion turbine EGUs; efficiency improvements reduce fuel burned per MWh and thus CO2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate design and operational measures such as increasing firing temperature, increasing pressure ratios, intercooling, inlet air cooling, matching high-efficiency HRSGs, using most efficient steam turbines, insulation, blowdown heat recovery, and best O&M practices (minimize steam leaks, air infiltration, maintain heat transfer surfaces). Consider demonstrated attainment of efficiency levels in recently constructed turbines and modest capital/compliance costs relative to alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency improvements for steam generating units (magnitude & limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency upgrades and operating practices for fossil-fired steam generating EGUs that may achieve CO2 emission rate reductions of roughly 0.1 to 5 percent for individual EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize these reductions are small relative to CCS and co-firing; explicitly weigh small per-unit gains against potential sectoral effects (including rebound). The EPA chose not to finalize efficiency improvements as BSER for any subcategory of existing coal-fired steam units because of small overall reductions and potential perverse outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of the rebound effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness that increasing efficiency can reduce marginal fuel cost and thereby increase utilization, potentially increasing total CO2 emissions (the "rebound effect").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating efficiency measures, assess whether increased utilization could offset per-MWh emission reductions. Do not assume efficiency gains always lower total emissions without modeling utilization changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of units with announced retirement or voluntary cessation
rubrics_metrics.description: Units that intend to cease operation before costs could be amortized should not be forced to bear substantial up-front capital expenditures (e.g., for CCS); EPA structured rules to avoid imposing costly obligations on such units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In BSER and cost-reasonableness determinations, consider announced retirement schedules and voluntary cessation plans. If a unit will retire before it could amortize control costs, controls may be infeasible or not cost-reasonable for that unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market, legislative, and state-policy context in feasibility assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of broader trends—fuel price dynamics, aging fleet, renewables growth, IIJA and IRA incentives, state RPS/CES, RGGI participation, and other market/regulatory drivers—when determining where BSER can be feasibly and cost-reasonably deployed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RIA and TSD modeling and external analyses (EIA projections) to account for how sectoral transition affects cost-effectiveness and deployability of controls. Financial incentives and state policies alter deployment economics and should inform EPA's BSER conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of federal incentives (IRA / IIJA) on deployment feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that IIJA and IRA provide substantial investments, tax credits, and incentives (e.g., increased 45Q values, 45V clean hydrogen credits, direct payment/transfer options) that materially reduce costs and accelerate CCS and related technology adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor statutory incentive design (credit levels, eligibility conditions, direct payment/transferability, construction start deadlines, capture design capacity thresholds such as 75% of baseline for 45Q) into assessments of cost-reasonableness and expected uptake of CCS/clean-hydrogen projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER focus on measures improving performance of individual sources
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's determination of BSER focused on 'measures that improve the pollution performance of individual sources,' not on generation technologies that serve as alternatives to fossil-fired EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When framing emission limitations and BSER, prioritize source-level controls and practices (e.g., CCS retrofit, co-firing, improved turbine efficiency) rather than shifting generation mix as the primary BSER measure, although system-level incentives are relevant contextual factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of utility IRPs and corporate commitments as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrated Resource Plans (IRPs) and publicly announced utility commitments to reduce GHGs (e.g., net-zero by 2050) demonstrate planned strategies like retirements, replacements with renewables/storage, and CCS deployment considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider IRPs and voluntary commitments as corroborating evidence of feasible industry behavior and planned investments; analyze filings and commitments to gauge how owners/operators will respond to regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-specific legal/regulatory requirements affecting controls
rubrics_metrics.description: State statutes, mandatory targets, tax incentives, and permitting rules (e.g., California SB 100 and SB 905, Montana's >=50% capture acquisition restriction, RGGI participation, Wyoming CCS incentives) influence feasibility and deployment of CCS and other controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate state law constraints and incentives into BSER analyses. State prohibitions (e.g., on EOR use of captured CO2) and mandatory targets affect available compliance pathways and market demand for captured CO2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated deployment and maturity of efficient generation technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficient generation technologies and best operating and maintenance practices have been in use for decades such that many recently constructed turbines have achieved the efficiency levels EPA is finalizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical deployment and recent construction performance data to support claims of technological maturity and realistic expectations for efficiency improvements with modest incremental costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and sizing requirements for tax credits/incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility thresholds and design capacity requirements (e.g., 45Q requirement that a qualifying carbon capture facility have CO2 capture design capacity of not less than 75 percent of the baseline CO2 production and construction must begin before Jan 1, 2033) affect which projects can monetize incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess projects against statutory eligibility criteria, capture thresholds, and construction/start deadlines to determine whether financial incentives materially change project economics and thereby influence BSER feasibility.
